Cross-reference to #maths > Fast computation of Bernoulli numbers @ 💬 :

https://github.com/nomeata/lean-cwp/ explores ways to do computation rather fast and still get a kernel-checkable proof of it.

Exciting!
It's somewhat reminiscent to reflection. What are the differences?

Here the proof term is built bit by bit, so the kernel has less to check. Empirically this sometimes performs better in lean, for instance mathlib's ring is implemented in this mindset in contrast to Rocq's ring by reflection, since this performed better in lean 3. I think it's unclear at the moment (to me) which strategy performs best in lean, but Joachim's project above means we can now experiment and benchmark significantly more easily

I would actually say that this is somewaht complementary by reflection. The core idea of proof by reflection is to run a computation to decide a property, and the computation is verified once and for all. Usually when we talk about proof by reflection, “run” here means kernel reduction (or, in the case of bv_decide, native evaluation). But it could also be “self-certifying evaluation” as in this experiment, and still plug into the machinery of proof by reflection that, well, reflects a goal into a domain-specific data structure and runs decisions procedures on that data structure.
